texts.preamble: I.M.Selvaraj vs The Food Safety Officer on 8 January, 2018 Author: V.Bharathidasan Bench: V.Bharathidasan Before The Madurai Bench Of Madras High Court Dated: 08.01.2018 Coram The Honourable Mr.Justice V.Bharathidasan W.P(MD)No.122 of 2018 and W.M.P.(MD).No.129 of 2018 I.M.Selvaraj ... Petitioner Vs. 1.The Food Safety officer, Code No.0451 Ramanathapuram, Tamil Nadu Food Safety and Drug Administration Department, O/o. Designated Officer, Ramanathapuram District Opposite to Hockey stadium District Collector Office, Ramanathapuram ? 623 504. 2.The Adjudicating Authority, The District Revenue Officer, Ramanathapuram District. ... Respondents Prayer: Writ Petition filed under Article 226 of the Constitution of India praying for issuance of a Writ of Certiorari, to call for the records relating to the impugned proceedings in Na.Ka.J5/3181/2017 pending before the second respondent and quash the same. !For Petitioner : Mr.M.Rajaraman For Respondents : Mr.M.Rajarajan Government Advocate :Order
texts.facts: This writ petition has been filed challenging the complaint filed by the first respondent under Section 51 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 (herein called as Act). The above complaint has been given by the first respondent on the ground that the petitioner is manufacturing and selling lighting oil. On inspection, the above oil has been seized by the first respondent and sample oil was sent for chemical examination before the Food Analyst. On examination of the oil, the Food Analyst has given an opinion that the sample oil is substandard. Based on the report the complaint has been filed under Section 3(1)(zx) of Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.
texts.arguments: 2. Heard, Mr.M.Rajaraman, learned counsel for the petitioner and Mr. M.Rajarajan, Government Advocate appearing for the respondents. 3.The learned counsel appearing for the petitioner submitted that the petitioner is only selling lighting oil and it is not edible oil and therefore, the question of substandard as contemplated under section 3(1)(zx) of the Act does not arise. Hence, no prima facie case is made out against the petitioner and the petitioner is not liable for any prosecution and the complaint has to be [LEAKAGE_MASK]. 4.The learned Government Advocate appearing for the respondents submitted that the petitioner is selling substandard product as gingelly oil, in the name of lighting oil. In the above circumstances, the oil was seized and sample oil was sent to Food Analyst and got an opinion from the laboratory wherein it is found that sample oil is substandard. 5. Considering the above facts and circumstances, as rightly contended by the learned Government Advocate for the respondent that the first respondent has filed a complaint under Section 51 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, on the ground that the petitioner is selling oil which is substandard and it is found that the presence of palmolein oil in the sample seized by the respondent and the petitioner did not follow the specified standards required for gingelly oil. 6. It is the contention of the petitioner that the petitioner is only selling a lighting oil which is not a gingelly oil. But the second respondent has considered the same as gingelly oil and wrongly come to the conclusion that the petitioner is selling a substandard gingelly oil and filed a complaint under section 3(1)(zx) of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 and sought to quash the above proceedings.
